latin: IN Nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti. Amen.
notes: Two-line drop I in the Latin column; the following N is an ordinary capital, given here as IN. The Latin column prints a cross between `Patris,` and `et Filii`; the cross glyph is not reproduced. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Ant. Introibo ad altare Dei. R. Ad Deum, qui lætificat juventutem meam.
notes: The Latin marks the antiphon `Ant.` in italic; antiphon and response are separate paragraphs, joined here as one block to match the sibling English row. This first occurrence prints a comma after `Ad Deum` which the repetition on xvi does not.

latin: JUDICA me Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab homine iniquo et doloso erue me. R. Quia tu es Deus, fortitudo mea, quare me repulisti? et quare tristis incedo, dum affligit me inimicus?
notes: Two-line drop J with `UDICA` in capitals, given here as JUDICA. The book prints `Judica`, with J, and `erue`, not `eripe`; both are transcribed as printed and no comparison with the 1962 typical edition is asserted here. The opening verse carries no speaker mark, the response does.

latin: P. Emitte lucem tuam, et veritatem tuam: ipsa me deduxerunt, et adduxerunt in Montem sanctum tuum, et in Tabernacula tua. R. Et introibo ad altare Dei: ad Deum qui lætificat juventutem meam.
notes: Runs over the page break xv/xvi: the response breaks after `ad Deum qui` at the foot of xv and `lætificat juventutem meam.` opens xvi. `Montem` and `Tabernacula` capitalised as printed.

latin: P. Confitebor tibi in cithara Deus Deus meus: quare tristis es, anima mea, et quare conturbas me? R. Spera in Deo, quoniam adhuc confitebor illi: salutare vultus mei, et Deus meus.
notes: The Latin sets `Deus Deus meus` with no comma between. The word breaks `ci-thara` at the line end and the `c` of `thara` is thinned by heavy inking on this leaf; the word is whole.

latin: P. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. R. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
notes: The Latin sets the doxology in full where the facing English abbreviates its first half to `and to, &c.` `sæcula sæculorum` with the ae-ligature, not `secula`. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Introibo ad altare Dei. R. Ad Deum qui lætificat juventutem meam.
notes: The antiphon repeated after the psalm, marked `P.` here where the first occurrence on xv is marked `Ant.`, and printing no comma after `Ad Deum` where the first occurrence prints one.

latin: P. Adjutorium nostrum in nomine Domini. R. Qui fecit cœlum et terram.
notes: `Adjutorium` with j, and `cœlum` with the oe-ligature, not `caelum`.

latin: P. Confiteor Deo omnipotenti, &c.
notes: The priest's Confiteor is abbreviated by `&c.` in the Latin column exactly as in the English; the full prayer is NOT obtainable from this element, and nothing is supplied. Only the ministers' form at seq 14 is set out in full.

latin: R. Misereatur tui omnipotens Deus, et dimissis peccatis tuis, perducat te ad vitam æternam. P. Amen.
notes: The ministers' response to the priest's Confiteor. The Latin sets `P. Amen.` on a line of its own, with `Amen.` italic.

latin: R. Confiteor Deo omnipotenti, beatæ Mariæ semper Virgini, beato Michaeli Archangelo, beato, Joanni Baptistæ, sanctis Apostolis Petro et Paulo, omnibus sanctis, et tibi Pater, quia peccavi nimis cogitatione, verbo et opere, mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa. Ideo precor beatam Mariam semper Virginem, beatum Michaelem Archangelum, beatum Joannem Baptistam, sanctos Apostolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes sanctos, et te Pater, orare pro me ad Dominum Deum nostrum.
notes: Runs over the page break xvi/xvii, breaking after `sanctis Apostolis Petro`. The Latin prints a spurious comma in `beato, Joanni Baptistæ`, transcribed as printed. No word `Catholicam` or `Catholicum` occurs: the list runs from `sanctis Apostolis Petro et Paulo` straight to `omnibus sanctis, et tibi Pater`. `mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa` is italic. Heavy inking at the head of xvii fills the e of `et` in `et Paulo` and breaks the m of `omnibus`; both words are whole and are read from the surviving strokes, not repaired from any other book.

latin: P. Misereatur vestri omnipotens Deus, et dimissis peccatis vestris, perducat vos ad vitam æternam. R. Amen.
notes: The priest's form of the Misereatur, answered `R. Amen.` where the ministers' form at seq 13 is answered `P. Amen.` `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Indulgentiam, absolutionem, et remissionem peccatorum nostrorum, tribuat nobis onmipotens et misericors Dominus. R. Amen.
notes: The Latin column misprints `onmipotens` for `omnipotens`, the m and n transposed; it is transcribed as printed and not corrected. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Deus tu conversus vivificabis nos. R. Et plebs tua lætabitur in te.
notes: `lætabitur` with the ae-ligature.

latin: P. Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam. R. Et salutare tuum da nobis.
P. Domine, exaudi orationem meam. R. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
notes: The Latin prints a comma after `Domine` where the facing English prints none after `O Lord`.

latin: P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo.
notes: The Latin response prints its full stop here; the facing English response at this block does not.

latin: Aufer a nobis quæsumus Domine, iniquitates nostras: ut ad Sancta Sanctorum, puris mereamur mentibus introire. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
notes: The Latin sets the conclusion `Per Christum Dominum nostrum.` in full where the facing English abbreviates it `Thro'.` `quæsumus` with the ae-ligature. `Amen.` italic. No comma is printed after `quæsumus`.

latin: Oramus te Domine per merita sanctorum tuorum, quorum reliquiæ hic sunt, et omnium sanctorum: ut indulgere digneris omnia peccata mea. Amen.
notes: `reliquiæ` with the ae-ligature. No comma after `te`. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Kyrie eleison, R. Kyrie eleison, P. Kyrie eleison.
notes: Set across the full measure, not in facing columns: the Greek acclamations stand in roman with the italic English gloss `Lord, have mercy upon us.` following on the same line. The acclamations are carried here with their speaker marks; the italic English gloss is omitted from this Latin artifact and stands in the sibling English row.

latin: R. Christe eleison, P. Christe eleison, R. Christe eleison.
notes: Set across the full measure like the preceding block; the italic English gloss `Christ, have mercy upon us.` is omitted here and stands in the sibling English row. The ministers begin this set.

latin: P. Kyrie eleison, R. Kyrie eleison, P. Kyrie eleison.
notes: The third set of three, opening xix, identical in wording to the first; set across the full measure with the italic English gloss omitted here as at seq 26.

latin: GLORIA IN EXCELSIS.
notes: The book's own Latin heading, centred across the full measure in roman capitals over both columns; the book supplies no English form of it, and the sibling English row carries the same Latin words for want of one.

latin: GLORIA in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis. Laudamus te; benedicimus te; adoramus te; glorificamus te. Gratias agimus tibi propter magnam gloriam tuam, Domine Deus, Rex cœlestis, Deus Pater omnipotens. Domine Fili unigenite Jesu Christe. Domine Deus, Agnus Dei, Filius Patris, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis. Qui tollis peccata mundi, suscipe deprecationem nostram. Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris, miserere nobis. Quoniam tu solus sanctus. Tu solus Dominus. Tu solus altissimus, Jesu Christe, cum Sancto Spiritu, in gloria Dei Patris. Amen.
notes: Two-line drop G with `LORIA` in capitals, given here as GLORIA. `bonæ` and `Rex cœlestis` with the ae- and oe-ligatures. `Jesu Christe` with J. `Amen.` italic.

latin: P. Dominus vobiscum. R. Et cum spiritu tuo.
notes: The last block on xix, introducing the Collect.
